a.description: The **Anchor** element creates a hyperlink to web pages, files, email addresses, locations on the same page, or anything else a URL can address.

abbr.description: The **Abbreviation** element represents an abbreviation or acronym. The optional `title` attribute provides an expansion or description.

address.description: The **Address** element indicates that the enclosed HTML provides contact information for a person or organization.

area.description: The **Area** element defines a hot-spot region on an image and optionally associates it with a hypertext link. Used inside `<map>`.

article.description: The **Article** element represents a self-contained composition in a document, page, application, or site, which is intended to be independently distributable or reusable (e.g., forum post, blog entry, news story).

aside.description: The **Aside** element represents a portion of a document whose content is only indirectly related to the document's main content. Frequently used for sidebars.

audio.description: The **Audio** element embeds sound content in documents. It may contain one or more `<source>` elements with different audio sources.

b.description: The **Bring Attention To** element draws the reader's attention to the element's contents. Use when no other more specific element fits (e.g., `<strong>`, `<em>`, `<mark>`).

base.description: The **Base** element specifies the base URL to use for all relative URLs in a document. There can be only one per document, inside `<head>`.

bdi.description: The **Bidirectional Isolate** element tells the browser's bidirectional algorithm to treat the text it contains in isolation from its surroundings.

bdo.description: The **Bidirectional Text Override** element overrides the current directionality of text, so that the text within is rendered in a different direction.

blockquote.description: The **Block Quotation** element indicates that the enclosed text is an extended quotation. Use the `cite` attribute for the source URL.

body.description: The **Body** element represents the content of an HTML document. There can be only one `<body>` element in a document.

br.description: The **Line Break** element produces a line break in text (carriage-return). It is useful for writing a poem or an address, where the division of lines is significant.

button.description: The **Button** element is an interactive element activated by a user with a mouse, keyboard, finger, voice command, or other assistive technology. Once activated, it performs an action such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.

canvas.description: The **Canvas** element is used with the Canvas API or WebGL API to draw graphics and animations. Provide fallback content between the tags.

caption.description: The **Table Caption** element specifies the caption (or title) of a table. Must be the first child of a `<table>` element.

cite.description: The **Citation** element is used to mark up the title of a cited creative work (book, paper, poem, movie, etc.).

code.description: The **Code** element displays its contents styled to indicate that the text is a short fragment of computer code. For multi-line code blocks, wrap in `<pre>`.

col.description: The **Table Column** element defines a column within a table and is used for defining common semantics on all common cells. Found within `<colgroup>`.

colgroup.description: The **Table Column Group** element defines a group of columns within a table.

data.description: The **Data** element links a given piece of content with a machine-readable translation via the `value` attribute.

datalist.description: The **Data List** element contains a set of `<option>` elements that represent the permissible or recommended options available to choose from within other controls.

dd.description: The **Description Details** element provides the description, definition, or value for the preceding `<dt>` element inside a `<dl>` description list.

del.description: The **Deleted Text** element represents a range of text that has been deleted from a document. Use `<ins>` for inserted text.

details.description: The **Details** disclosure widget creates a widget that shows/hides additional information. The `<summary>` child provides the visible label.

dfn.description:
The **Definition** element specifies a term that is going to be defined within the content. The nearest parent `

`, `

`/`
` pair, or `
` is the definition context.

dialog.description: The **Dialog** element represents a dialog box or other interactive component, such as a dismissible alert, inspector, or subwindow. Use `showModal()` for modal behavior.

div.description: The **Content Division** element is the generic container for flow content. It has no effect on content or layout until styled with CSS.

dl.description: The **Description List** element represents a description list. It encloses a list of groups of terms (using `<dt>`) and descriptions (using `<dd>`).

dt.description: The **Description Term** element specifies a term in a description or definition list. Must be used inside a `<dl>` element, usually followed by `<dd>`.

em.description: The **Emphasis** element marks text that has stress emphasis. Nesting `<em>` elements increases the level of emphasis.

embed.description: The **Embed** element embeds external content at the specified point in the document. This content is provided by an external application or other source of interactive content.

fieldset.description: The **Field Set** element is used to group several controls as well as labels within a web form. Use `<legend>` as the first child for a caption.

figcaption.description: The **Figure Caption** element represents a caption or legend describing the rest of the contents of its parent `<figure>` element.

figure.description: The **Figure** element represents self-contained content, potentially with an optional caption specified using `<figcaption>`. Commonly used for images, code snippets, diagrams.

footer.description: The **Footer** element represents a footer for its nearest ancestor sectioning content or sectioning root element. Typically contains author info, copyright, related links.

form.description: The **Form** element represents a document section containing interactive controls for submitting information. Use `action` for the submission URL and `method` for HTTP method.

h1.description: **Heading level 1** — the highest section heading level. Use only one `<h1>` per page for the main topic.

h5.description: **Heading level 5** — rarely used deep section heading.

h6.description: **Heading level 6** — the deepest (least important) section heading.

head.description: The **Head** element contains machine-readable information (metadata) about the document, like its title, scripts, and style sheets. Not visible to users.

header.description: The **Header** element represents introductory content, typically a group of introductory or navigational aids. May contain heading, logo, search form.

hgroup.description: The **Heading Group** element represents a multi-level heading for a section. It groups `<h1>`–`<h6>` elements, treating the first as the primary heading.

hr.description: The **Horizontal Rule** element represents a thematic break between paragraph-level elements: e.g., a scene change in a story, or a shift of topic within a section.

html.description: The **HTML** element represents the root (top-level element) of an HTML document. All other elements must be descendants of this element. Always include `lang` attribute.

i.description: The **Idiomatic Text** element represents a range of text set off from the normal text for some reason (technical terms, foreign phrases, thoughts, etc.).

iframe.description: The **Inline Frame** element represents a nested browsing context, embedding another HTML page into the current one. Always provide a `title` for accessibility.

img.description: The **Image** element embeds an image into the document. Always provide `alt` text for accessibility. Use `loading="lazy"` for off-screen images.

input.description: The **Input** element creates interactive controls for web-based forms. The `type` attribute determines the control: text, password, email, number, checkbox, radio, file, etc.

ins.description: The **Inserted Text** element represents a range of text that has been added to a document. Use `<del>` for deleted text.

kbd.description: The **Keyboard Input** element represents a span of inline text denoting textual user input from a keyboard, voice input, or any other text entry device.

label.description: The **Label** element represents a caption for an item in a user interface. Associating a `<label>` with a form control improves accessibility and usability.

legend.description: The **Fieldset Legend** element represents a caption for the content of its parent `<fieldset>`. Must be the first child.

li.description: The **List Item** element represents an item in a list. Must be contained in an ordered list (`<ol>`), unordered list (`<ul>`), or menu (`<menu>`).

link.description: The **External Resource Link** element specifies relationships between the current document and an external resource. Most commonly used for CSS stylesheets.

main.description: The **Main** element represents the dominant content of the `<body>` of a document. There should be only one `<main>` per page (excluding hidden ones).

map.description: The **Image Map** element is used with `<area>` elements to define an image map (a clickable link area on an image).

mark.description: The **Mark** element represents text which is marked or highlighted for reference or notation purposes due to the passage's relevance in the enclosing context.

menu.description: The **Menu** element represents a group of commands that a user can perform or activate. This includes both list menus (toolbar) and context menus.

meta.description: The **Metadata** element represents metadata that cannot be represented by other HTML meta-related elements (`<base>`, `<link>`, `<script>`, `<style>`, `<title>`).

meter.description: The **Meter** element represents either a scalar value within a known range or a fractional value. Used for disk usage, relevance scores, etc.

nav.description: The **Navigation** Section element represents a section of a page whose purpose is to provide navigation links, either within the current document or to other documents.

noscript.description: The **No Script** element defines a section of HTML to be inserted if a script type on the page is unsupported or if scripting is turned off in the browser.

object.description: The **Object** element represents an external resource, which can be treated as an image, a nested browsing context, or a resource to be handled by a plugin.

ol.description: The **Ordered List** element represents an ordered list of items — typically rendered as a numbered list. Use `type` for numbering style (1, A, a, I, i).

optgroup.description: The **Option Group** element creates a grouping of options within a `<select>` element. Use `label` for the group name.

option.description: The **Option** element defines an item contained in a `<select>`, an `<optgroup>`, or a `<datalist>` element.

output.description: The **Output** element is a container into which a site or app can inject the results of a calculation or the outcome of a user action.

p.description:
The **Paragraph** element represents a paragraph. Paragraphs are block-level elements; they automatically close if another block element is encountered before the closing `

`.

picture.description: The **Picture** element contains zero or more `` elements and one `` element to offer alternative versions of an image for different display/device scenarios.

pre.description: The **Preformatted Text** element represents preformatted text which is to be presented exactly as written in the HTML file. Whitespace is preserved.

progress.description: The **Progress** element displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task, typically displayed as a progress bar.

q.description: The **Inline Quotation** element indicates that the enclosed text is a short inline quotation. Browsers typically insert quotation marks around it.

rp.description: The **Ruby Fallback Parenthesis** element provides fallback parentheses for browsers that do not support ruby annotations. Used inside `<ruby>`.

rt.description: The **Ruby Text** element specifies the ruby text component of a ruby annotation, used for East Asian typography. Used inside `<ruby>`.

ruby.description: The **Ruby** element represents small annotations that are rendered above, below, or next to base text (usually for East Asian characters showing pronunciation).

s.description: The **Strikethrough** element renders text with a strikethrough, indicating things that are no longer relevant or accurate. Use `<del>` for document edits.

samp.description: The **Sample Output** element represents sample (or quoted) output from a computer program.

script.description: The **Script** element embeds executable code or data (typically JavaScript). Use `src` for external scripts and `defer` for non-blocking loading.

search.description: The **Search** element represents a part of the document that contains form controls or other content related to a search or filtering operation.

section.description: The **Section** element represents a generic standalone section of a document, which doesn't have a more specific semantic element to represent it.

select.description: The **Select** element represents a control that provides a menu of options. Use `multiple` for multi-select and `size` for visible rows.

slot.description: The **Slot** element — part of the Web Components technology suite — is a placeholder inside a web component that you can fill with your own markup.

small.description: The **Small** element represents side-comments and small print, like copyright and legal text, independent of its styled presentation.

source.description: The **Media Source** element specifies multiple media resources for `<picture>`, `<audio>`, or `<video>` elements. Use `srcset`+`media` for responsive images.

span.description: The **Span** element is a generic inline container for phrasing content, which does not inherently represent anything. Use it to group elements for styling.

strong.description: The **Strong Importance** element indicates that its contents have strong importance, seriousness, or urgency. Browsers typically render the contents in bold type.

style.description: The **Style** element contains style information (CSS) for a document, or part of a document. For external stylesheets, use `<link>` instead.

sub.description: The **Subscript** element specifies inline text which should be displayed as subscript for solely typographical reasons (e.g., H₂O).

summary.description: The **Disclosure Summary** element specifies a summary, caption, or legend for a `<details>` element's disclosure box. Must be the first child.

sup.description: The **Superscript** element specifies inline text which is to be displayed as superscript for solely typographical reasons (e.g., x², footnotes).

svg.description: The **SVG** element is a container that defines a new coordinate system and viewport. It is used as the outermost element of SVG documents embedded in HTML.

table.description: The **Table** element represents tabular data — information presented in a two-dimensional table comprised of rows and columns.

tbody.description: The **Table Body** element encapsulates a set of table rows (`<tr>`), indicating that they comprise the body of the table.

td.description: The **Table Data Cell** element defines a cell of a table that contains data. Use `colspan` and `rowspan` for spanning cells.

template.description: The **Template** element holds HTML that is not rendered immediately when a page is loaded but may be instantiated during runtime using JavaScript.

textarea.description: The **Textarea** element represents a multi-line plain-text editing control. Use `rows` and `cols` for size; use CSS `resize` to control resizability.

tfoot.description: The **Table Foot** element defines a set of rows summarizing the columns of the table. Must appear after `<thead>`, before `<tbody>`.

th.description: The **Table Header Cell** element defines a cell as header of a group of table cells. Use `scope` attribute for accessibility (`col`, `row`, `colgroup`, `rowgroup`).

thead.description: The **Table Head** element defines a set of rows defining the head of the columns of the table.

time.description: The **Time** element represents a specific period in time. Use `datetime` attribute to translate dates into machine-readable format.

title.description: The **Title** element defines the document's title that is shown in a browser's title bar or a page's tab. Required in every HTML document.

tr.description: The **Table Row** element defines a row of cells in a table. The row's cells can then be established using a mix of `<td>` and `<th>` elements.

track.description: The **Embed Text Track** element is used as a child of `<audio>` or `<video>` to specify timed text tracks (subtitles, captions, descriptions, chapters).

u.description: The **Unarticulated Annotation** element represents a span of inline text which should be rendered with a non-textual annotation (underline). Use for Chinese proper names or misspelled words.

ul.description: The **Unordered List** element represents an unordered list of items, typically rendered as a bulleted list.

var.description: The **Variable** element represents the name of a variable in a mathematical expression or a programming context.

video.description: The **Video** element embeds a media player which supports video playback into the document. Use `<source>` for multiple formats, include `controls` for playback UI.

wbr.description: The **Word Break Opportunity** element represents a position within text where the browser may optionally break a line. Used for long URLs or code.

class.description: A space-separated list of the CSS classes of the element. Classes allow CSS and JavaScript to select and access specific elements via the class selector or `document.getElementsByClassName`.

id.description: Defines a unique identifier (ID) which must be unique in the whole document. Its purpose is to identify the element when linking (fragment identifier), scripting, or styling with CSS.

style.description: Contains CSS styling declarations to be applied to the element. Note that it is recommended for styles to be defined in separate files. Inline styles have the highest specificity.

title.description: Contains text representing advisory information related to the element it belongs to. Typically displayed as a tooltip on mouse hover.

lang.description: Specifies the primary language of the element's contents and for any of the element's attributes that contain text. Use BCP 47 language tags (e.g., `en`, `ko`, `ja`, `fr`, `de`).

dir.description: Specifies the text direction of the element's content. Values: `ltr` (left-to-right), `rtl` (right-to-left), or `auto` (browser determines).

tabindex.description: Allows developers to make an element focusable (allow or prevent sequential focus navigation). `0` = normal tab order, `-1` = not reachable via tab but focusable via script, positive = custom tab order (avoid).

accesskey.description: Provides a hint for generating a keyboard shortcut for the current element. The shortcut consists of Alt+key (Windows/Linux) or Ctrl+Option+key (Mac).

contenteditable.description: An enumerated attribute indicating if the element should be editable by the user. Values: `true` (editable), `false` (not editable), or `plaintext-only` (editable with plain text only).

draggable.description: Enumerated attribute indicating whether the element can be dragged using the Drag and Drop API. Values: `true` (draggable), `false` (not draggable).

hidden.description: Boolean global attribute indicating that the element is not yet, or is no longer, relevant. The browser won't render hidden elements. Do not use to hide visible content — use CSS instead.

spellcheck.description: Enumerated attribute defines whether the element may be checked for spelling errors. Values: `true` (check), `false` (don't check). Defaults to browser behavior.

translate.description: Enumerated attribute that specifies whether an element's translatable attribute values and text node children should be translated when the page is localized. Values: `yes` or `no`.

data-*.description: Custom data attributes allow proprietary information to be exchanged between HTML and its DOM representation via scripts. The `*` can be replaced by any name following XML naming rules (e.g., `data-user-id="42"`).

role.description: ARIA role attribute. Defines the explicit ARIA role of the element for assistive technologies. Common roles: `button`, `navigation`, `banner`, `main`, `complementary`, `dialog`, `alert`, `tabpanel`.

aria-label.description: Defines a string value that labels an interactive element. Used when no visible text label exists. Essential for accessibility when an element has no text content but conveys meaning visually.

aria-hidden.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to the accessibility API. `true` = hidden from screen readers, `false` = visible. Use for purely decorative content.

aria-describedby.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object. Similar to `aria-labelledby`, but for descriptive text rather than a label.

aria-labelledby.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element. Used when a visible text label is present elsewhere in the document.

aria-expanded.description: Set on an element to indicate whether a control is expanded or collapsed and whether its child elements are displayed or hidden. Used for accordions, dropdowns, etc.

aria-controls.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element. Used for tabs, accordions, etc.

href.description: The URL that the hyperlink points to. Used on `<a>`, `<area>`, `<base>`, `<link>` elements. Can be an absolute URL, relative URL, fragment (`#id`), or JavaScript (`javascript:void(0)`).

src.description: The URL of the embeddable content. Used on ``, `

alt.description: Defines an alternative text description of the image. Required for accessibility — screen readers read this text. Leave empty (`alt=""`) for purely decorative images.

type.description: Defines the type of the element. For `<input>`: text, password, email, number, tel, url, search, date, checkbox, radio, file, submit, reset, button, color, range. For `<script>`: MIME type (default: `text/javascript`).

name.description: Name of the element. For form controls, this is used as the key when submitting form data. For `<iframe>`, it sets a targetable name for the browsing context. For `<meta>`, sets the metadata name.

value.description: Defines the default value for the element. For `<input>`: initial value. For `<button>`, `<option>`: the value submitted with the form. For `<li>` (in `<ol>`): sets the list item's ordinal number.

placeholder.description: Provides a hint to the user of what can be entered in the field. Disappears when the user starts typing. Should not be used as a replacement for `<label>`.

disabled.description: Boolean attribute: if present, the form control is not mutable, focusable, or submitted with the form. Applies to `<button>`, `<fieldset>`, `<input>`, `<optgroup>`, `<option>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`.

required.description: Boolean attribute: if present on an `<input>`, `<select>`, or `<textarea>`, the user must specify a value before the form can be submitted.

readonly.description: Boolean attribute: if present on `<input>` or `<textarea>`, the value is not editable by the user but is still submitted with the form. The element can still receive focus.

checked.description: Boolean attribute: if present on `<input type=checkbox>` or `<input type=radio>`, the element is checked (toggled on) by default.

selected.description: Boolean attribute: if present on an `<option>` element, the option is initially selected when the page loads. Only one `<option>` in a single-select should have this.

multiple.description: Boolean attribute: if present on `<input type=file>` or `<select>`, the user may select more than one value.

autofocus.description: Boolean attribute: if present, the element should automatically receive focus when the page loads (or when the `<dialog>` it's in is shown). Only one element per document should have `autofocus`.

autocomplete.description: Specifies whether the browser should provide autocomplete suggestions. Values: `on`, `off`, or specific tokens like `name`, `email`, `tel`, `new-password`, `current-password`, `street-address`, etc.

maxlength.description: The maximum string length (in UTF-16 code units) that the user can enter into the field. Constraint validation. For `<input>` and `<textarea>`.

minlength.description: The minimum string length (in UTF-16 code units) that the user can enter. Constraint validation. For `<input>` and `<textarea>`.

min.description: The minimum value accepted by the element. For `<input>` (type number, range, date, etc.) and `<meter>`.

max.description: The maximum value accepted by the element. For `<input>` and `<meter>`. Must be greater than or equal to `min`.

step.description: The granularity that the value must adhere to. For `<input>` (number, range, date, etc.). Defaults to 1 for numeric types.

pattern.description: A regular expression that the control's value is checked against. For `<input>`. The pattern must match the entire value (not just a substring). Use `title` to describe the expected pattern.

accept.description: For `<input type=file>`, specifies which file types the server accepts. Values: MIME types (e.g., `image/*`), file extensions (`.pdf,.doc`), or `audio/*`, `video/*`, `image/*`.

target.description: Specifies where to display the linked URL. Values: `_self` (same frame), `_blank` (new tab/window), `_parent`, `_top`. For `<a>`, `<area>`, `<base>`, `<form>`.

rel.description: Specifies the relationship between the current document and the linked resource. Common values: `stylesheet`, `icon`, `preload`, `nofollow`, `noopener`, `noreferrer`, `alternate`, `canonical`. For `<a>`, `<area>`, `<link>`, `<form>`.

action.description: The URL that processes the form submission. For `<form>`. If omitted, the form submits to the current page URL.

method.description: The HTTP method to submit the form with. Values: `GET` (data in URL query string), `POST` (data in request body), or `dialog` (closes dialog without submitting). For `<form>`.

enctype.description: The MIME type used to encode form data. Values: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (default), `multipart/form-data` (for file uploads), `text/plain`.

width.description: Specifies the width of the element in CSS pixels. For ``, `

height.description: Specifies the height of the element in CSS pixels. For ``, `

for.description: Specifies which form element a `<label>` is bound to. Must match the `id` of the target element. Also used on `<output>` to list element ids that contributed to the calculation.

rows.description: The number of visible text lines for the `<textarea>` control. Default is 2.

cols.description: The visible width of the `<textarea>` text control, in average character widths. Default is 20.

wrap.description: Indicates how the `<textarea>` control wraps text for form submission. Values: `hard` (adds line breaks), `soft` (no line breaks, default).

loading.description: Indicates how the browser should load the resource. Values: `eager` (immediately), `lazy` (defer until near viewport). For `` and `

decoding.description: Provides an image decoding hint to the browser. Values: `sync` (decode synchronously), `async` (decode asynchronously to avoid blocking), `auto` (default, no preference).

srcset.description: One or more strings separated by commas, indicating possible image sources for the user agent to use. Each string is composed of a URL followed by a width descriptor or pixel density descriptor.

sizes.description: One or more strings separated by commas, indicating a set of source sizes. Each source size consists of a media condition followed by a size value. Used with `srcset`.

media.description: Specifies a media condition (similar to a media query) for `<source>`, `<link>`, `<style>`, `<a>`. The resource is only used if the condition matches.

controls.description: Boolean attribute: if present on `<audio>` or `<video>`, the browser offers controls to allow the user to control playback (play, pause, volume, seeking).

autoplay.description: Boolean attribute: if present on `<audio>` or `<video>`, the media automatically begins playback as soon as it can, without waiting for the entire file to load.

loop.description: Boolean attribute: if present on `<audio>` or `<video>`, the media player will automatically seek back to the start upon reaching the end.

muted.description: Boolean attribute: if present on `<audio>` or `<video>`, the audio output will be muted. Useful with `autoplay` since many browsers block unmuted autoplay.

poster.description: A URL for an image to be shown while the video is downloading, or until the user hits the play button. For `<video>`. If not specified, the first frame is used.

scope.description: Defines the cells that the `<th>` header element relates to. Values: `row`, `col`, `rowgroup`, `colgroup`. Essential for table accessibility.

colspan.description: Specifies the number of columns a `<td>` or `<th>` cell should span. Default is 1. Values higher than 1000 are clamped.

rowspan.description: Specifies the number of rows a `<td>` or `<th>` cell should span. Default is 1. Values higher than 65534 are clamped.

cite.description: Contains a URL which points to the source of the quotation or edit. For `<blockquote>`, `<q>`, `<del>`, `<ins>`. Not rendered visually by browsers.

datetime.description: Indicates the date and time associated with the element. For `<time>`: a machine-readable format for the human-readable content. For `<del>`/`<ins>`: the date the change was made.

async.description: Boolean attribute for `<script>`: if present, the script is fetched in parallel and executed as soon as it is available (potentially before HTML parsing completes).

defer.description: Boolean attribute for `<script>`: if present, the script is fetched in parallel and executed after the page has finished parsing. Has no effect on inline scripts.

charset.description: Declares the character encoding of the document. Must be present on the `<meta charset="utf-8">` element. Should always be UTF-8.

content.description: The value of the metadata. For `<meta name="description" content="...">`: the page description shown in search results. For `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`: responsive viewport settings.

http-equiv.description: Defines a pragma directive. Values: `content-security-policy`, `content-type`, `default-style`, `refresh`, `x-ua-compatible`. For `<meta>`.
